arxiv-1704-08286.title: The first syzygy of Hibi rings associated with planar distributive lattices Thanks: AMS Classification 2010. Primary: 05E40, 06D75, 03G10, 16E05
arxiv-1704-08286.creator: Priya Das, Himadri Mukherjee
arxiv-1704-08286.description: Abstract . In this article, we give explicit minimal generators of the first syzygy of the Hibi ring for a planar distributive lattice in terms of sublattices. We also give a characterization when it is linearly related and derive an exact formula for the first Betti number of a planar distributive lattice. 1.

arxiv-2006-13152.title: Magnify Your Population: Statistical Downscaling to Augment the Spatial Resolution of Socioeconomic Census Data Conference: KDD Workshop on Humanitarian Mapping; August 24, 2020; accepted KDD Workshop on Humanitarian Mapping, August 24, 2020
arxiv-2006-13152.creator: Giulia Carella, Andy Eschbacher, Dongjie Fan, Miguel Álvarez, Álvaro Arredondo, Alejandro Polvillo Hall, Javier Pérez Trufero, Javier de la Torre
arxiv-2006-13152.description: Abstract Abstract Fine resolution estimates of demographic and socioeconomic attributes are crucial for planning and policy development. While several efforts have been made to produce fine-scale gridded population estimates, socioeconomic features are typically not available at scales finer than Census units, which may hide local heterogeneity and disparity.

arxiv-2210-11294.title: Neutrinoless double-beta decay at colliders: interference between Majorana states
arxiv-2210-11294.creator: Jonathan L. Schubert, Oleg Ruchayskiy
arxiv-2210-11294.description: Abstract Heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) are hypothetical particles able to explain several puzzles of fundamental physics, first and foremost — neutrino oscillations. Being sterile with respect to Standard Model interactions, these particles admit Majorana masses, allowing for violation of the total lepton number. Lepton number violating (LNV) processes thus become a key signature of HNLs, pursued by many experiments.

arxiv-2212-04724.title: Characterization of production sets through individual returns-to-scale: a non parametric specification and an illustration with the U.S industries
arxiv-2212-04724.creator: Jean-Philippe Boussemart, Walter Briec, Raluca Parvulescu, Paola Ravelojaona
arxiv-2212-04724.description: Abstract This paper proposes to estimate the returns-to-scale of production sets by considering the individual return of each observed firm through the notion of Λ \Lambda -returns to scale assumption. Along this line, the global technology is then constructed as the intersection of all the individual technologies.

arxiv-2311-11193.title: Assessing AI Impact Assessments: A Classroom Study
arxiv-2311-11193.creator: Nari Johnson, Hoda Heidari
arxiv-2311-11193.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nari Johnson, Hoda Heidari. Artificial Intelligence Impact Assessments (“AIIAs”), a family of tools that provide structured processes to imagine the possible impacts of a proposed AI system, have become an increasingly popular proposal to govern AI systems. Recent efforts from government or private-sector organizations have proposed many diverse instantiations of AIIAs, which take a variety of forms ranging from open-ended questionnaires to graded score-cards. However, to date that has been limited evaluation of existing AIIA instruments.

arxiv-2311-18727.title: Automatic Functional Differentiation in JAX
arxiv-2311-18727.creator: Min Lin
arxiv-2311-18727.description: Abstract We extend JAX with the capability to automatically differentiate higher-order functions (functionals and operators). By representing functions as a generalization of arrays, we seamlessly use JAX’s existing primitive system to implement higher-order functions. We present a set of primitive operators that serve as foundational building blocks for constructing several key types of functionals.

arxiv-2402-17747.title: When Your AIs Deceive You: Challenges of Partial Observability in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
arxiv-2402-17747.creator: Leon LangUniversity of Amsterdam, Davis FooteUC BerkeleyStuart RussellUC Berkeley Anca Dragan UC Berkeley Erik Jenner UC Berkeley, Scott Emmons UC Berkeley
arxiv-2402-17747.description: Abstract Past analyses of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) assume that the human evaluators fully observe the environment. What happens when human feedback is based only on partial observations? We formally define two failure cases: deceptive inflation and overjustification. arxiv-2509-14447.title: Biologically Plausible Online Hebbian Meta-Learning: Two-Timescale Local Rules for Spiking Neural Brain Interfaces
arxiv-2509-14447.creator: Sriram V.C. Nallani, Gautham Ramachandran, Sahil Shah
arxiv-2509-14447.description: Abstract Brain-Computer Interfaces face challenges from neural signal instability and memory constraints for real-time implantable applications. We introduce an online SNN decoder using local three-factor learning rules with dual-timescale eligibility traces that avoid backpropagation through time while maintaining competitive performance.

arxiv-2511-12738.title: Direct Visual Grounding by Directing Attention of Visual Tokens
arxiv-2511-12738.creator: Parsa Esmaeilkhani, Longin Jan Latecki
arxiv-2511-12738.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Parsa Esmaeilkhani, Longin Jan Latecki. Vision Language Models (VLMs) mix visual tokens and text tokens. A puzzling issue is the fact that visual tokens most related to the query receive little to no attention in the final layers of the LLM module of VLMs from the answer tokens, where all tokens are treated equally, in particular, visual and language tokens in the LLM attention layers. This fact may result in wrong answers to visual questions, as our experimental results confirm.

arxiv-2511-20902.title: A Taxonomy of Pix Fraud in Brazil: Attack Methodologies, AI-Driven Amplification, and Defensive Strategies
arxiv-2511-20902.creator: Glener Lanes Pizzolato, Brenda Medeiros Lopes, Claudio Schepke, Diego Kreutz
arxiv-2511-20902.description: Abstract This work presents a review of attack methodologies targeting Pix, the instant payment system launched by the Central Bank of Brazil in 2020. The study aims to identify and classify the main types of fraud affecting users and financial institutions, highlighting the evolution and increasing sophistication of these techniques.

pmc-11416181.description: The financial costs associated with publishing in academic journals have steadily risen in recent years, reflected by higher publishing fees and the emergence of open access (OA) publishing models. Research remains an essential part of academia and has special significance for residency applicants.

pmc-11463776.title: Barriers and enablers that influence the uptake of HIV testing among heterosexual migrants in the Netherlands
pmc-11463776.creator: Veronica Martinez Martinez, Hermen Ormel, Eline L. M. Op de Coul
pmc-11463776.description: BackgroundHeterosexual migrant men and women in the Netherlands often face barriers to accessing health services, including HIV testing, that may lead to late-stage HIV diagnoses. This study explored factors of influence in the usage of HIV testing among heterosexual migrants.

pmc-11712687.title: SAA‐Determined α‐Synuclein in Early AD ADNI Participants: Contribution to cognitive trajectories from a sex differences perspective
pmc-11712687.creator: Marta Milà‐Alomà, Zachary Hausle, Tamar M Schaap
pmc-11712687.description: Backgroundα‐synuclein (αSyn) aggregates are a common co‐pathology in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and can be identified in CSF with high reliability using the Seed Amplification Assay (SAA). While AD prevalence and impact on cognition are higher in women, the opposite pattern is found for α‐synucleinopathies.

pmc-12359519.title: Reducing syndemics of non-communicable chronic diseases in Mayan Indigenous population through community-based participatory research: a mixed-methods study protocol
pmc-12359519.creator: Emilio Motte-García, Cinthya Cadena-Trejo, María Fernanda Ramírez-Flores, Alfonso Gastelum Strozzi, Adalberto Loyola-Sanchez, María Victoria Fernandez-Garcia, Karen G Castillo-Hernandez, Kenia Nayrobi López-Herrera, Maarten M H Lahr, Erik Buskens, Ingris Pelaez-Ballestas
pmc-12359519.description: BackgroundIndigenous Mayan-Yucatecan communities in Mexico have a high prevalence of chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) such as diabetes, hypertension, obesity and rheumatic diseases (RMDs). According to the syndemic theory, these diseases combined with social, economic and cultural factors affect the quality of life.

pmc-12382506.title: Neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade: a new treatment option for patients with early-stage mismatch repair deficient solid tumors
pmc-12382506.creator: Kristin G Anderson, Antoni Ribas
pmc-12382506.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). DNA mismatch repair deficiency has been identified as a biomarker that strongly correlates with tumor response to anti-programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) checkpoint blockade therapy in the metastatic setting. In a promising Phase 2 study published in the New England Journal of Medicine, Cercek et al demonstrate that PD-1 checkpoint blockade also has potential in the neoadjuvant setting and may eliminate the need for surgical intervention.

pmc-12582870.title: The effects of 12 weeks of plyometric training on body composition, physical strength, and bone mineral density in obese adolescents
pmc-12582870.creator: Seung Jin Han, Jean Kyung Paik, Myungchul Kim, Jun-Su Kim
pmc-12582870.description: This study aimed to investigate the effects of 12 weeks of plyometric training on body composition, physical fitness, and bone mineral density (BMD) in obese male adolescents. Twenty obese male adolescents were randomly assigned to a control group (n=10) or a plyometric exercise group (n=10). The plyometric exercise group performed the exercise 3 times a week for 12 weeks.

pmc-12660927.title: DDNet: disaster damage detection for buildings based on dual-temporal joint attention network
pmc-12660927.creator: Xiaosan Ge, Lin Zhou, Di Meng
pmc-12660927.description: Rapid and accurate assessment of building damage is crucial for effective post-disaster emergency response. The use of pre-disaster and post-disaster satellite imagery is a common approach for detecting building damage. This task involves two essential subtasks: building localization and damage classification.

Hamers, the INTERACT Study Group
pmc-13084184.description: IntroductionIndonesia has an escalated HIV epidemic among key populations, especially men who have sex with men (MSM). Diagnosis and immediate treatment of acute HIV infection (AHI), the earliest phase with the highest transmission risk, is beneficial for individual health and can reduce onward transmission.

pmc-13088993.title: Minimal Change Disease Following B-Cell Maturation Antigen–Directed Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy
pmc-13088993.creator: Kiran Shivaraj, Omar Mamlouk, Amanda Tchakarov, Krina Patel, Ala Abudayyeh
pmc-13088993.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a well-recognized complication of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, typically attributed to cytokine release syndrome and acute tubular injury. However, glomerular disease post CAR-T cell is rare. We report a case of minimal change disease presenting with AKI and nephrotic-range proteinuria 3 weeks after B-cell maturation antigen–directed CAR-T cell therapy, ciltacabtagene autoleucel, in a patient with relapsed refractory multiple myeloma.

pmc-13224650.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). pmc-13251258.title: Hematological and leukocyte morphometric indices as low-cost diagnostic adjuncts in acute coronary syndromes
pmc-13251258.creator: Mansi Mehrotra, Dushyant Singh Gaur, Kunal Gururani, Mansi Kala
pmc-13251258.description: ObjectiveAcute Coronary Syndromes (ACS) remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly in resource-limited settings where access to advanced diagnostics may be constrained. This study aimed to evaluate the utility of routine hematological indices and leukocyte morphometric parameters—volume, conductivity, and scatter (VCS)—as low-cost adjuncts for identifying ACS and differentiating its subtypes.

pmc-13286962.title: Modeling multiscale neural dynamics for EEG-based emotion recognition using an attentive wavelet–transformer framework
pmc-13286962.creator: R. S. Soundariya, P. Thangaraj
pmc-13286962.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Electroencephalography (EEG)-based emotion recognition faces challenges such as signal noise, non-stationarity, inter-subject variability, and class imbalance, limiting its practical application in affective computing and clinical diagnostics. This study introduces the Attentive Wavelet-Transformer Network (AWT-Net), a novel framework integrating Hierarchical Wavelet Packet Decomposition (HWPD), Empirical Wavelet Transform with Kalman filtering (EWT-Kalman), Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA), and a Hybrid Spatio-Temporal Transformer (HSTT) to address these issues.

pmc-13458088.title: Clinical outcomes of carbapenem vs. non-carbapenem therapy in hospitalized adults with shigellosis
pmc-13458088.creator: Zach Zhang, Gregory B. Tallman, Brian Kendall, Emily Fox
pmc-13458088.description: Background:Management of shigellosis is increasingly complicated by antimicrobial resistance, yet susceptibility testing is rarely performed, and the role of broad-spectrum empiric therapy in hospitalized adults remains unclear.Methods:We conducted a multi-center retrospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with stool-confirmed Shigella spp. from October 2023 to August 2024 across five hospitals in the Portland metropolitan area.

pmc-13527636.title: Case Report: A Previously Healthy Young Woman With Lethal, Unremitting Metabolic Acidosis: Could a Novel Variant in ALAS2 Be the Culprit?
pmc-13527636.creator: Greg Brown, Stephen Brown
pmc-13527636.description: BackgroundHeme synthesis is critical for several biological processes, including mitochondrial energy production and oxygen delivery via hemoglobin. The initial and rate‐limiting step in heme synthesis is the conjugation of glycine with succinyl‐CoA to form 5‐aminolevulinic acid (ALA), which is catalyzed by two closely related enzymes that are coded by highly homologous genes, known as ALAS1 and ALAS2.

pmc-13624452.title: Gamification in dental education: Role of Kahoot in enhancing student engagement, learning outcomes and knowledge retention
pmc-13624452.creator: Afsheen Mansoor, Fouzia Farrukh, Emaan Mansoor, Shabana Ali
pmc-13624452.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objective:Digital technology in education has made a significant change in pedagogy where Gamification has become a novel approach of instruction involving competition, scoring, rewards and leaderboards that is capable of enhancing motivation and engagement of learners. Kahoot is the most widely used online game-based learning platform that not only create interactive quizzes but also conduct real-time testing which amplifies learning of educators.
